feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: American Muslims are giving Texas barbecue a halal makeover
entry.summary: Even as anti-Muslim rhetoric rises in Texas, Muslim pitmasters are winning over diners and reshaping one of the state's most iconic culinary traditions.

entry.title: U.S. envoys Witkoff and Kushner land for talks in Kyiv after meeting Putin in Moscow
entry.summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to arrive in Kyiv on Sunday in their first visit to the Ukrainian capital as part of a renewed push for peace in Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

entry.title: QUIZ: Ugh, I'll do it later. How much do you know about procrastination?
entry.summary: Learn a few surprising facts about procrastination — and helpful tools to overcome it — with this quiz. It's based on social scientist Itamar Shatz's new book, Solving Procrastination.

entry.title: Whatever happened to kindness? Spoiler alert: Our readers prove it's alive and well
entry.summary: We asked readers to share stories about a moment of kindness involving a stranger. Here are some of their heartwarming anecdotes.

entry.title: Jazz legend John Coltrane's Philadelphia house to become a cultural heritage site
entry.summary: On the centennial of father's birth, Ravi Coltrane talks about turning the home where the jazz legend spent a crucial period in the 1950s into a cultural heritage and community space.

entry.title: U.S. and Iran trade attacks on ships as fighting flares up again
Opinion: A sculpture in perpetual motion, removed
entry.summary: "Blue," a statue that's been on the grounds of the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C. for 7 years has been dismantled and removed.

entry.title: Trump administration to dig at triumphal arch site despite no final federal approvals
entry.summary: The Trump administration says it will break ground on a 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington, D.C., without final federal approval and despite an ongoing lawsuit.

entry.title: U.S.-Venezuela oil deal puts opposition in a political bind
entry.summary: Venezuelan opposition members are uneasy with new oil deals with the U.S., worried that agreements with authoritarian regime in Caracas could undermine democratic progress.

entry.title: Whatever happened to the floating schools of Bangladesh?
entry.summary: It was a light bulb moment: If monsoon rains keep kids from safely getting to school, let's create a floating school to pick them up! Bangladesh pioneered the idea. How's it doing?
